Hakainde Hichilema is bidding for second term, but feud between him and family of Edgar Lungu, who died in 2025, continues

As Zambians go to the polls on Thursday, the ghost of the current president’s predecessor hangs over the elections.

Hakainde Hichilema, 64, is bidding for a second term leading the southern African country after defeating his arch-rival Edgar Lungu by a landslide in 2021.

guardian.description:
Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake

At least 44 people have died after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, police said.

The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales.

Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

guardian.description:
The Comac C919 will fly from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, although experts say it could take generations for it to challenge the west’s dominance of the industry

China hopes to break into the world of commercial aviation with the first international flight of a Chinese-made passenger jet scheduled for Wednesday.

The Comac C919 will take off from Beijing capital international airport at 3pm, landing in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, just over two hours later.

euronews.description: Spain has logged five months in a row of annual inflation above 3%, driven by dearer electricity and fuel as the partial closure of the Strait of Hormuz persists. In July, power prices top €100 per MWh, the highest year-on-year figure since 2022.

euronews.title: Soaring stingray numbers off California beaches drive record injuries
euronews.description: California is seeing unusually large numbers of round stingrays near its beaches, as warmer coastal waters and an expected strong El Niño draw the animals closer to shore.

euronews.description: A group of wild boar was spotted at night roaming the streets of Setúbal, even crossing a busy road, as their growing presence prompts the council to urge caution.

euronews.title: Timelapse of partial solar eclipse seen from Royal Observatory Greenwich
euronews.description: Britain witnessed its most significant solar eclipse since 1999, with more than 90% of the Sun obscured in some parts of the country. Crowds gathered in parks and open spaces to watch the rare celestial event. In London, the sky turned an eerie grey as a sliver of sunlight appeared above the Moon.

euronews.title: Tokyo issues angry response as Putin makes his first visit to the disputed Kuril islands
euronews.description: The four contested islands, seized by Russia during World War II, have gained importance since the end of the conflict, providing strategic military bases to the Kremlin, coupled with their rich mineral deposits and fishing grounds.

euronews.title: Colombia: "scene of horror" as Pereira rescuers search rubble
euronews.description: Colombia's earthquake death toll rose to 265 in Pereira by 12 August 2026, with almost 500 still missing. Rescuers described scenes of horror as the critical 72-hour survival window closed.

euronews.title: Which way for EU enlargement? Brussels faces moment of truth over bloc's expansion
euronews.description: EU enlargement is set to face its moment of truth in the coming months as Montenegro and Albania near membership, Ukraine and Moldova advance, and Brussels weighs reforms needed to absorb a bigger, more complex Union.

euronews.title: 'The best night of my life' Travis Kelce shares first thoughts on intimate wedding to Taylor Swift
euronews.description: American footballer Travis Kelce has revealed his feelings about becoming one with Taylor Swift in his first comments on his secretive marriage to the pop sensation.

euronews.title: Half a million visitors flock to Spain’s path of total solar eclipse
euronews.description: Spain witnessed its first total solar eclipse in more than a century on Wednesday 12 August, drawing millions of people to viewing sites across the north of the country as the Moon passed directly in front of the Sun.

euronews.title: The EU loses one in four litres of treated water. Can digitalisation fix that?
euronews.description: Global water demand will increase by 55 percent by 2050. Europe loses 23 percent of treated water before it's billed because of old, leaky pipes. Water Europe says AI-driven upgrades could generate around €3 billion in annual savings and more than 13,000 jobs.

euronews.title: Rare eclipse plunges parts of Europe into darkness
euronews.description: Skywatchers across Europe gathered to watch a rare solar eclipse, using protective glasses as the Moon passed in front of the Sun.

euronews.description: From the digital euro to private interoperability and Brazil's PIX, the race for sovereignty is on, but the real test is securing payment autonomy at home and abroad.

rfi.title: Can UK's hard-right Farage bin financial probe with by-election win?
rfi.description: Nigel Farage – leader of the anti-immigration Reform UK party – will be fighting for his parliamentary seat on Thursday, going head to head with parody candidate Count Binface in snap polls. The by-election was called after Farage resigned amid a probe into his finances. But the surprise move threatens to backfire as none of the major political parties has fielded a candidate.

rfi.title: Millions gaze as solar eclipse plunges swathe of Spain into darkness
rfi.description: The total eclipse plunged a vast swathe of Spain from broad daylight into darkness Wednesday, drawing awed gasps and applause from spectators gathered in parks and cities across the country.

rfi.title: Voters in Zambia to deliver verdict on president's economic record
rfi.description: Zambia are voting in a general election on Thursday which will decide whether President Hakainde Hichilema returns for a second term, after steering the country out of a debt crisis.

rfi.title: French ambassador to CAR disciplined over misconduct allegations
rfi.description: France’s foreign ministry has launched disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to the Central African Republic, following allegations that he repeatedly brought young women to the official residence in Bangui and had sexual relations with some of them.

rfi.title: Iran faces growing isolation and uncertain future amid 'dire' economic situation
rfi.description: As economic pressure mounts in Iran, RFI spoke to economist Djamchid Assadi about how this is leaving the country more isolated and strengthening the role of the Revolutionary Guards.

rfi.title: Russia threatens retaliatory seizures of EU ships amid new sanctions push
rfi.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for plans to sell off cargo seized from Russian "shadow fleet" vessels.

rfi.title: France gripped by latest summer heatwave as drought conditions worsen
rfi.description: Scorching heat continued to spread across most of mainland France on Wednesday, as the Ministry for Ecological Transition met to take stock of the effects of a drought that has been steadily worsening since May.

rfi.title: Hungary elects Orban critic Andras Baka as first president in new political era
rfi.description: Hungarian lawmakers on Tuesday approved former supreme court chief Andras Baka – a prominent critic of Viktor Orban who was ousted during the ex-premier's time in power – as the country's next head of state.

rfi.title: Assisted dying, social media and agriculture put France’s top court in spotlight
rfi.description: France’s Constitutional Council is facing a politically charged end to the summer, with judges due to rule on a series of high-profile laws – including those covering assisted dying, social media use by children, agriculture and public security.

rfi.title: Lebanon becomes first country in Middle East to abolish death penalty
rfi.description: Lebanon’s parliament on Tuesday abolished the death penalty, making it the first country in the Middle East to replace capital punishment with a sentence of life imprisonment with hard labour.

rfi.title: Former Syrian leader Assad sentenced to death in absentia over war crimes
rfi.description: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death after a trial in absentia, convicting him of atrocities committed during the country's civil war. Six of his closest aides were also handed death sentences.

rfi.title: Race to find Ebola vaccine as DR Congo outbreak kills more than 2,000
rfi.description: The latest outbreak of Ebola has killed more than 2,000 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to health authorities. Meanwhile, international efforts have been stepped up to test a vaccine for the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever.

rfi.title: France and EU join international aid effort after Colombia earthquake
rfi.description: France has joined the European Union and a host of countries in offering assistance to Colombia, where volunteers and rescuers are searching for survivors following Monday's deadly earthquake.

rfi.title: May ’68 protest leader Cohn-Bendit pledges support to Glucksmann for 2027
rfi.description: Former Green MEP Daniel Cohn-Bendit, a historic figure on the French left, on Monday gave his support to Raphaël Glucksmann for France’s 2027 presidential election, in an interview with Le Point magazine.

rfi.title: Rebel forces in Ethiopia's Tigray state condemn army drone strikes
rfi.description: Rebel authorities on Tuesday accused the Ethiopian government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in southern Tigray state and condemned the move as "a serious escalation", amid fears of a new war.

rfi.title: France introduces tough fines for unsolicited telemarketing calls
rfi.description: France has banned unsolicited telemarketing calls under a new law to protect consumers and shield vulnerable people from fraudulent commercial practices. Individuals who make illegal calls can be fined up to €75,000 per call when the new law comes into effect on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Iran says ‘Muslim Nato’ pact reflects retreat from US security umbrella
rfi.description: Tehran has played down concerns over a new mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, while portraying the agreement as evidence of declining regional reliance on the United States.

rfi.title: Moscow and Damascus reach deal over Russian military bases in Syria
rfi.description: Syria said on Sunday it had reached a deal with Moscow on the fate of Russia's two bases in the country, which it once used to provide military support to ousted leader Bashar al-Assad during the Syrian civil war.

lemonde.title: Fabien Barthez, champion du monde 1998, nommé entraîneur des gardiens dans l’encadrement de Zinédine Zidane

lemonde.title: La Roumanie procède à l’arrêt complet de l’unique centrale nucléaire du pays à cause du faible débit du Danube
lemonde.description: La mise à l’arrête complète de la centrale nucléaire de Cernavoda, qui fournit habituellement un cinquième de la production totale d’électricité du pays, constitue une première depuis la canicule de 2003.

france24fr.description: Des millions de personnes ont assisté, émerveillées, à l'éclipse solaire totale qui a plongé dans l'obscurité une partie de l'Islande ​et de l'Espagne mercredi.

france24fr.title: Royaume-Uni : Nigel Farage face à Tête-de-poubelle dans une législative hors du commun
france24fr.description: Nigel Farage, chef du parti anti-immigration Reform UK, espère jeudi être largement réélu lors d'une législative partielle en Angleterre, qu'il a lui-même déclenchée, où il a pour principal rival Count Binface, candidat fantaisiste portant une poubelle sur la tête.

france24fr.title: CAN féminine: le Malawi affrontera le Cameroun pour la première finale de son histoire
france24fr.description: Le Malawi s'est qualifié pour la finale de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations féminine pour sa première participation en éliminant l'Algérie (3-1), mercredi à Rabat, dans une demi-finale jouée pendant 45 minutes à 10 contre 10. Elle affrontera le Cameroun, vainqueur contre le Maroc.

france24fr.title: Fabien Barthez intègre l'encadrement des Bleus version Zidane
france24fr.description: La Fédération française de football a officialisé, jeudi, l'intégration de Fabien Barthez dans le nouvel encadrement des Bleus après la nomination de Zinedine Zidane en tant que sélectionneur. L'ancien portier international, champion du monde avec l'équipe de France en 1998, s'occupera de l'entraînement spécifique des gardiens.

france24fr.title: La quasi-totalité de la France placée en vigilance orange canicule jusqu'à vendredi
france24fr.description: La vague de chaleur se poursuit, jeudi, en France avec 80 départements placés en vigilance orange canicule jusqu'à vendredi inclus. Le gouvernement chiffre jusqu'à 15 milliards d'euros le coût de ces phénomènes de chaleur extrême successifs cet été.

france24fr.title: Ukraine en direct : juillet, mois le plus meurtrier pour les civils depuis mai 2022
france24fr.description: Le mois de juillet a été le plus meurtrier pour les civils en Ukraine depuis mai 2022, après quatre ans et demi d'invasion russe, selon un rapport publié jeudi par l'ONU. Au moins 437 civils ont été tués et 2 610 blessés, soit une hausse de 30 % par rapport à juin et de 70 % par rapport à juillet 2025. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Législative partielle au Royaume-Uni : Nigel Farage opposé au candidat Tête-de-poubelle
france24fr.description: Nigel Farage, chef du parti anti-immigration Reform UK, espère être largement réélu, jeudi, lors d'une législative partielle en Angleterre. Lors de ce scrutin, qu'il a déclenché, il a pour principal rival Count Binface, candidat fantaisiste portant une poubelle sur la tête.

france24fr.title: Première visite de Vladimir Poutine aux îles Kouriles, le Japon "proteste vigoureusement"
france24fr.description: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine s'est rendu pour la première fois, jeudi, dans les îles Kouriles en Extrême-Orient. Cette visite a provoqué une vive protestation du Japon, qui revendique également cet archipel.

france24fr.title: Vainqueur d'Aston Villa, le PSG conserve son titre en Supercoupe d'Europe
france24fr.description: Le Paris Saint-Germain a lancé sa saison en s'imposant contre Aston Villa (2-1) en Supercoupe d'Europe, mercredi soir à Salzbourg. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia et Désiré Doué ont trouvé le chemin des filets pour le double champion d'Europe en titre.

france24fr.title: Au Venezuela, gouvernement et opposition esquissent un accord sur une réforme de la justice
france24fr.description: Le pouvoir et l'opposition vénézuéliens ont conclu, mercredi, leur premier cycle de dialogue, s'accordant sur un processus de réforme judiciaire et la récupération d'actifs gelés au Royaume-Uni. Même si les États-Unis ne sont pas à la table des négociations, ils sont très présents dans les discussions et ont été sollicités à plusieurs reprises comme "médiateurs" lors de points d'achoppement.

france24fr.title: En Colombie, la fenêtre de tir pour retrouver des survivants du séisme se referme
france24fr.description: Les recherches de survivants en Colombie entrent dans leur phase critique, jeudi, à l'approche du délai de 72 heures après le séisme de magnitude 7,4, qui a fait au moins 265 morts et des centaines de disparus, selon un dernier bilan. Le président a décrété trois jours de deuil national et l'urgence économique.

france24fr.title: En Zambie, des élections à valeur de test pour le bilan économique du président sortant "HH"
france24fr.description: Près de 8,7 millions de Zambiens sont appelés aux urnes, jeudi, pour choisir leur président. Le chef d'État sortant Hakainde Hichilema, salué pour son redressement économique, affronte l'opposant Brian Mundubile, qui accuse le gouvernement d'avoir entravé sa campagne.

france24fr.title: Éclipse totale en Espagne : au sommet de la cathédrale de Ségovie, 59 secondes hors du temps (4/4)
france24fr.description: À Ségovie, en Espagne, l’éclipse totale de Soleil a plongé la ville dans l’obscurité pendant 59 secondes, mercredi soir. Depuis les rues comme du sommet de la cathédrale, habitants et visiteurs ont assisté, bouleversés, à la disparition du Soleil.

france24fr.title: Pétrolier échoué au large d'Oman : la marée noire a atteint les côtes
france24fr.description: Les fuites d'un pétrolier échoué au large d'Oman, soupçonné d'appartenir à la flotte fantôme russe, ont atteint les côtes omanaises, menaçant jusqu'à 40 kilomètres de rives. La mousson complique les opérations pour contenir cette marée noire, qui menace une réserve naturelle protégée.

france24fr.title: Karoline Leavitt, porte-parole de la Maison Blanche et trumpiste convaincue, quitte son poste
france24fr.description: Karoline Leavitt, porte-parole de la Maison Blanche, quittera ses fonctions à la fin du mois pour consacrer davantage de temps à son rôle de maman. spiegel.description: Vernachlässigung und Gewalt: Die Jugendämter in Deutschland haben 2025 zehn Prozent mehr Kindeswohlgefährdungen gemeldet als im Jahr zuvor. Was über die Fälle bekannt ist.

spiegel.title: Hipp-Erpressung: Rattengift in Babynahrung – wie der mutmaßliche Erpresser ausgeforscht wurde
spiegel.description: Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen steht der Erpressungsversuch des deutschen Babynahrung-Herstellers vor der Aufklärung. Österreichs Ex-Staatsschutzchef spielt eine Schlüsselrolle bei den Ermittlungen.

spiegel.title: Pete Hegseth: US-Verteidigungsminister kündigt gemeinsame Militäreinsätze mit Kolumbien an
spiegel.description: Kolumbien tritt dem von Washington geführten Antidrogenbündnis bei und soll die USA um gemeinsame Einsätze gegen Kartelle gebeten haben. Verteidigungsminister Hegseth prahlte mit der Ankündigung eines harten Vorgehens.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn stattet weiteres Personal an Bahnhöfen mit Bodycams aus
spiegel.description: Bodycams sollen Bahn-Beschäftigte vor Übergriffen schützen. Nach dem Zugpersonal sollen nun auch mehr Mitarbeiter an Bahnhöfen die kleinen Videokameras tragen können.

spiegel.title: Roman »Kaskaden« von Louise K. Böhm: Kann man eine Freundschaft je hinter sich lassen?
spiegel.description: Jojo und Yara waren zwei gegen die Welt. Und heute? Im Roman »Kaskaden« geht es um Freundschaft, Liebe und Kapitalismus. Ein starkes Debüt.

spiegel.title: Flughafen Leipzig/Halle: Sprengstoffdrohne legt deutsche Verwundbarkeit offen
spiegel.description: Der Leipziger Flughafen entging nur knapp einer Katastrophe. Der versuchte Anschlag mit einer Sprengstoffdrohne zeigt, wie verwundbar Deutschland ist. Die Behörden haben nach SPIEGEL-Informationen inzwischen kaum mehr Zweifel: Hinter der Attacke dürfte Moskau stecken.

spiegel.title: Supercup: Paris Saint-Germain holt Titel gegen Aston Villa
spiegel.description: Paris Saint-Germain gewinnt den Uefa-Supercup – und bereitet Aston Villa dabei mehr Probleme als Omar Artan. Der Schiedsrichter aus Somalia durfte die Partie leiten, nachdem ihm zur WM die Einreise verweigert worden war.

spiegel.title: Thailand: Tourist aus Deutschland stirbt bei Badeunfall auf Phuket
spiegel.description: Ein deutscher Tourist ist in Thailand ums Leben gekommen. Dem 30-Jährigen wurde starker Wellengang zum Verhängnis. Rettungsteams fanden den Mann nach langer Suche leblos im Meer.

spiegel.title: Russland-Ukraine-Krieg: Kyjiw greift Schwarzmeerküste und Krim mit Drohnen an
spiegel.description: Kyjiw hat die russische Schwarzmeerküste und die annektierte Krim massiv mit Drohnen angegriffen. Unterdessen nannte Präsident Selenskyj eine konkrete Zahl im Zusammenhang mit Patriot-Raketen, die sein Land im Winter braucht.

spiegel.title: Rumänien will wegen Donau-Niedrigwasser einziges Atomkraftwerk Cernavodă herunterfahren
spiegel.description: Das rumänische AKW Cernavodă steht wegen Niedrigwassers in der Donau vor der Abschaltung. Auch in Frankreich ist die Stromproduktion durch gefallene Pegelstände beeinträchtigt. Ein weiterer Grund dort: eine Quallenplage.

spiegel.title: Wetter in Deutschland: Es wird wieder richtig heiß – bis zu 37 Grad erwartet
spiegel.description: Deutschland stehen die nächsten Hitzetage bevor. Für das Wochenende wird jedoch ein Wetterumschwung vorhergesagt, mit teils kräftigen Schauern und Gewittern.

observador.title: CPI a Luís Neves?  Paulo Muacho: "É um mecanismo que está...
observador.description: O deputado do Livre considera que Luís Neves é "um bom ministro" e prefere esperar pelos resultados da auditoria à PJ. Paulo Muacho faz balanço do mandato de Seguro e aborda (in)segurança em Lisboa.

observador.title: Insegurança em Lisboa resolve-se com mais videovigilância?
observador.description: Mulher baleada na Baixa relança tema da segurança. Manuel Lopes, da ADBP, fala em "caso isolado", mas pede videovigilância. Advogado Saragoça da Matta diz que, bem utilizada, "não viola a privacidade"

observador.title: As notícias das 10h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: "Tranca Segura": PJ detém 20 pessoas por tráfico de droga
observador.description: A rede usava métodos inusitados: pólen de haxixe transportado no corpo, cocaína num rolo de carne e drogas sintéticas impregnadas em supostas mensagens infantis.

observador.title: Nuno Melo e as fragatas: um negócio que meteu água?
observador.description: O Ministro e o Chega trocam mimos e processos por causa de navios e comissões fantasma. E ainda, o eclipse que humilhou a gestão pública e a caça aos 180 km/h declarada por Luís Neves.

observador.title: As notícias das 9h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Encontrado sem vida um dos 4 portugueses que naufragaram
observador.description: Foram retomadas às seis da manhã locais as operações de busca por dois portugueses após o naufrágio na Croácia. Autoridades encontraram um corpo.

observador.title: Consultas atrasadas e o rescaldo do eclipse
observador.description: Metade do total de primeiras consultas de especialidade do SNS não cumpriram tempos máximos. Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa já teve alta. E ainda as imagens do eclipse de ontem.

observador.title: Imagens das Perseidas. Após o eclipse, a chuva de meteoros
observador.description: Quarta-feira foi um dia cheio de fenómenos astronómicos e culminou com uma chuva de meteoros. As Perseidas foram fotografadas em Israel, Jordânia, Turquia e Sérvia, por exemplo.

observador.title: 100 anos de Fidel Castro, o ditador que enfeitiça a esquerda
observador.description: Nenhum ditador esteve tantos anos no poder como Fidel Castro, mas mesmo assim e com a evidência de tanta miséria em Cuba, a sua memória continua a enfeitiçar boa parte da esquerda. Porquê?

observador.title: Vila Franca de Xira agora tem um grito de revolta?
observador.description: Entre vernáculos populares na Assembleia e sussurros estranhos em aviões, a política anda a precisar de férias. Ou será que precisa de um técnico de ar condicionado que acalme os ânimos?

observador.title: Urgências. Tempos de espera aumentam em Lisboa e no Algarve
observador.description: Esta manhã doentes urgentes enfrentam esperas superiores a cinco horas em Lisboa e a duas no Algarve. Direção do SNS garante tempo está "dentro dos valores expectáveis". Ainda, Benfica joga na Escócia

observador.title: Ganhar um troféu ou apanhar o avião? Não perder dinheiro
observador.description: Fulham e Málaga disputaram um amigável que teminou empatado e teve ser o horário do voo de regresso da equipa inglesa a desempatar o jogo. Ainda, o eclipse que irritou uns e distraiu outros.

observador.title: Afinal a festa dos eclipses ainda não acabou?
observador.description: Até 2027 o calendário espacial está cheio com quase toda a "família" de fenómenos no céu. E ainda, o silêncio das aves e a calma dos mamíferos no Zoo de Lisboa durante o apagão solar.

observador.title: Há hospitais com 60% das consultas fora do prazo máximo
observador.description: Nos hospitais de Penafiel e Matosinhos, mais de dois terços das primeiras consultas não cumprem os tempos máximos. Hospital de Cascais tem o melhor desempenho. Primeiras consultas em quebra em 2026.

observador.title: "Diplomacia com Irão não é uma recompensa"
observador.description: Bruno Cardoso Reis sublinha que o diálogo com o Irão é uma necessidade estratégica perante o perigo de mísseis. Destaca ainda o plano de Zelensky contra Putin e o impasse militar de Israel no Líbano.

observador.title: Boeing condenada a pagar 25 milhões de euros em ação civil
observador.description: Júri federal de Chicago deu razão à viúva de Michael Ryan, funcionário da ONU morto no voo ET302 da Ethiopian Airlines. Dois processos relacionados com os acidentes do 737 MAX permanecem em aberto.

observador.title: Javalis na praia. As autoridades estão a fechar os olhos?
observador.description: Ninguém assume as culpas e as entidades atropelam-se em desculpas sobre a invasão na Arrábida. E a sina de improvisar na segurança e o adeus ao espetáculo do eclipse.

elpais.title: El eclipse conquista el corazón de España

elpais.title: El olvidado asombro de estar vivos
elpais.description: Siempre levanta ternura el hecho de que, cuando el ser humano no encuentra palabras para describir lo que está pasando, renuncie a buscarlas

elpais.title: Millones de españoles se maravillan con el eclipse de Sol: “¡Quiero otro!, ¿cuándo hay otro?”

elpais.title: ¿Te has perdido este eclipse? En 2027, el próximo le toca al sur andaluz, Ceuta y Melilla

elpais.description: Aunque millones de personas en España se volcaron para presenciar el primer fenómeno de este tipo en más de un siglo en la Península, muchos se lo perdieron por sus obligaciones laborales

elpais.title: España cifra en hasta 5.000 los migrantes de Ceuta que pueden ser acogidos
elpais.description: El Gobierno estima que 2.500 menores y unos 2.500 potenciales solicitantes de asilo siguen en la ciudad autónoma

elpais.title: Las Ketchup: “Fuimos muy mal asesoradas. A todos les daba igual que te doliera todo el cuerpo”

nyt.description: A shifting race and a key endorsement helped the moderate Democrat overcome his progressive challenger, Francesca Hong, voters said.

npr.title: Colombia's new government and rescuers race against the clock to find survivors

Scientists may begin with millions—or even billions—of antibody candidates, but only a tiny fraction will recognize and bind tightly to the disease target. Identifying those rare candidates has long been one of the biggest challenges in developing antibody medicines.

phys-org.title: Nature's original bioplastic may have fed animals for hundreds of millions of years
phys-org.description: Long before humans discovered biodegradable plastics, microorganisms had already invented their own. Many bacteria and archaea produce natural bioplastics called polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs), storing them inside their cells as reserves of carbon and energy.

phys-org.title: 'Imposing ignorance': US climate science under siege
phys-org.description: A benchmark U.S. report on the fast-changing state of the Arctic has been canceled. The nation's top research body has removed a chapter on global warming from a reference manual for judges.

phys-org.title: Germany's dry rivers spark battle over engineering vs. restoration
phys-org.description: As a heat wave dries Germany's rivers, government ministers are at odds over what to do about it—re-engineer the waterways or restore them to their natural state.

phys-org.title: Uniaxial strain reveals new way to tune electron flow in altermagnet material
phys-org.description: Altermagnetism is a new, third type of magnetism of great interest for spin-transport applications like computer memory. If properly harnessed, it could combine the benefits of the two existing types of magnetism, ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism, ultimately reducing or eliminating heat during information transfer and increasing the ability to miniaturize next-generation technologies. phys-org.title: A 236-million-year-old fossil challenges the story of mammalian live birth
phys-org.description: Some cynodonts may have been giving birth to live young much sooner in evolutionary history than previously assumed. A new Frontiers in Mammal Science study has offered the first compelling evidence that cynodonts may have been viviparous—a reproductive mode characterized by live birth.

phys-org.title: This South African river has a bacteria count off the charts: A natural filter is cleaning it for watering food gardens
phys-org.description: Every day, millions of liters of polluted water flow through many South African rivers and disappear into the sea.

phys-org.title: EU curbs on 'forever chemicals' in food packaging kick in
phys-org.description: New EU restrictions on toxic substances known as "forever chemicals" in food packaging kicked in Wednesday, along with broader rules aimed at cutting packaging waste in the bloc.

phys-org.title: African grasslands expanded 5 million year earlier than previously thought, molecular fossils suggest
phys-org.description: The iconic grassland savannas of Africa are geographically extensive and important for both local fauna and the global climate. But where did they come from, and how will they change in the future? Ongoing warming, rising CO2 levels and shifting rainfall patterns are likely to profoundly change these ecosystems. These effects are difficult to predict because they can alter ecosystems in competing ways.

phys-org.title: AI‑designed viruses are a test of whether biosecurity can keep pace
phys-org.description: Scientists have crossed an important line in biological engineering. In a recent study, researchers used artificial intelligence to design complete sets of genetic instructions for bacteriophages, viruses that infect bacteria. Some of those computer-generated designs produced working viruses when they were built and tested in the laboratory.

phys-org.title: Drug-carrying nanoparticles shrink venous malformations by 70% in mice
phys-org.description: Venous malformations are abnormally shaped veins that develop when the cells lining blood vessels grow too fast when they aren't supposed to. Children can be born with them, and as the child grows, the venous malformations can get bigger. Venous malformations are a type of vascular malformation that can range from small and superficial to disfiguring, debilitating or even life-threatening.

phys-org.title: Models of glacial collapse in Antarctica improve predictions of sea-level rise
phys-org.description: With approximately one-third of the world's population living within a day's walk of a coastline, sea-level rise poses a serious global threat. Every centimeter of sea-level rise could displace 1.5 million people, and current estimates range from half a meter (1.6 feet) to 2 meters (6.6 feet) by the end of the 21st century—which means that potentially hundreds of millions of people could be affected. phys-org.title: Unsupervised free time increases the likelihood that adolescents will engage in violent behavior, 21-country study finds
phys-org.description: A study involving more than 58,000 adolescents from 21 countries found that "unstructured free time"—defined as periods without adult supervision or activities guided by educational, cultural or athletic goals—is strongly associated with delinquent behavior and exposure to violence among young people.

phys-org.title: What it's like to discover an ancient Egyptian tomb, and the race against time to preserve it
phys-org.description: Looking inside a newly discovered ancient tomb for the first time is both exciting and terrifying. I was fortunate to experience this recently as director of an international research team carrying out fieldwork in the Theban necropolis, a UNESCO World Heritage Site near the modern Egyptian city of Luxor.

phys-org.title: Ultrafast flash Joule heating significantly reduces MXene manufacturing time
phys-org.description: MXenes are two-dimensional materials made of very thin layers of metals, measured on the atomic scale. They conduct electricity well and have surfaces that can easily interact with other materials, making them excellent candidates for advanced electronic devices, computers and aerospace coatings. The only problem is that, until a recent innovation by James Tour's lab at Rice University, building them required a lengthy, acid-filled process called liquid-phase chemical etching.

phys-org.title: Space travel doesn't affect the strength of heart muscle cells, study finds
phys-org.description: It's common to see images of astronauts on the International Space Station exercising, running on special treadmills and pedaling cycles designed for tight quarters.

phys-org.title: Graphene nanowrinkles could reshape electricity in future ultrathin devices
phys-org.description: Rice University researchers have shown that tiny wrinkles in graphene can change the material's electrical properties, providing evidence for flexoelectricity, a phenomenon in which a material generates an electric charge when it bends unevenly. The findings are published in Advanced Materials.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

proj-syn.title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
proj-syn.description: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
proj-syn.description: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

proj-syn.title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
proj-syn.description: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

proj-syn.title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
proj-syn.description: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.

proj-syn.title: The Last Trump Election
proj-syn.description: No matter what US President Donald Trump says or does in response to the results of this November’s midterms, he will have faced his final popular vote. There will be further damage done to public confidence in American democratic institutions, but the institutions themselves will hold.

proj-syn.title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration
proj-syn.description: When tens of thousands of people recently entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco, European leaders lapsed into recriminations, reigniting the debate on migration. But the bigger challenge is to address a long-simmering territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.

proj-syn.title: The Rising Price of a Cheap Renminbi
proj-syn.description: Renminbi appreciation would not, on its own, rebalance China’s economy and eliminate its massive surpluses. But by increasing households’ purchasing power over imports and compressing tradable-sector margins, it would raise the cost of avoiding reform.
